purpose: Ensures that every organizational user is uniquely identified and authenticated before being granted access to organizational systems.
summary: Each user has a unique identifier (no shared accounts for individual use), authentication uses an approved method (password policy, MFA), and privileged access requires an additional authentication factor.
expectedStatementElements: Confirmation that accounts are unique per user (no shared credentials)
What authentication factors are required (password policy specifics, MFA)
Whether privileged/administrative access requires MFA specifically
How authentication is enforced consistently across in-scope systems
How exceptions (e.g., service accounts) are documented and controlled
evidenceExamples: Identity provider configuration showing MFA enforcement
List of shared/service accounts with compensating controls
commonGaps: Statement doesn't confirm whether MFA is required for privileged access specifically
Shared or generic accounts not addressed or justified
No confirmation that the policy is enforced consistently, not just documented
interviewQuestions: Is MFA required for all users, or only privileged accounts?
Are there any shared or generic accounts, and how are they controlled?
How is this enforced technically, versus just written in policy?
